title: The Anatomy of a Perfect Star Rating
summary: This lesson covers essential UX improvements for star rating components, including hover previews, state management, and accurate data representation. It also demonstrates how micro-interactions like staggered animations and progress rings can enhance the user experience.

transcript.text: Your star rating is lying to your users.
Hover should preview. Hover fills the stars before you click. Most widgets only react after the click. Show the user where they're about to land.
Preview does not equal committed. Move the cursor away and it snaps back. Preview and selection are two different layers. Mix them up and the value flickers on every hover.
A 4.4 average is not five full stars. Rounded up and you're lying to people. Render the real fraction with a clipped half star.
The 30ms that feels alive. Fill them left to right, 30 milliseconds apart. That tiny stagger is the satisfying part. Pop them all at once and it feels dead.
Pair the discrete stars with one continuous ring. The arc reads faster than any number. Stars to rate, a ring to summarize.
Stop rounding up. Follow for more UI anatomy. Save this before you ship another rating.

on_screen_text: COMMITTED LAYER the real saved value
all at once: 0ms delay — flat, lifeless
30ms stagger: fills left to right — satisfying
Stars to rate, a ring to summarize.
design_principles: Redundant Coding (Using both stars and a ring for faster comprehension)
before_after: Transforms a basic, static star rating into an interactive, accurate, and polished component with hover previews and staggered animations.
